title_en: Djerba seawater desalination station (first in Tunisia)
attributed_to: Youssef Chahed, then head of government, at the kick-off ceremony on 2 May 2018 (Webmanagercenter/TAP): "méga-projet réalisé par des compétences tunisiennes moyennant des investissements d'environ 180 millions de dinars". An earlier SONEDE loan-guarantee law of March 2014 covered 120 MDT.
L'Economiste Maghrébin (2022-04-01), reporting the kick-off ceremony: JICA loan of 36.676 billion yen (~800 million dinars), 25-year maturity, 7-year grace, 1.7% interest.
L'Economiste Maghrébin/TAP (02/11/2023), quoting the project's reported completion date (end December 2023)

title_en: Solar Water PLC southern-Tunisia solar desalination proposal
attributed_to: Tunisian Ministry of Economy and Planning communiqué (via L'Economiste Maghrébin, 2022-12-01): estimated investment cost of 600 million euros for a 200,000 m3/day solar-powered desalination station in the Tunisian south, presented by Solar Water PLC to minister Samir Saied with UK ambassador Helen Winterton.

L'Economiste Maghrébin (N. Dejoui, 2024-06-13) reporting the Tunisia Investment Forum: Team Europe committed a total of 472.6 million euros to ELMED and its ecosystem. Components: EU Connecting Europe Facility grant 307.6 MEUR approved December 2022, grant agreement signed 7 August 2023 by CINEA, TERNA and STEG; EBRD/EIB/KfW loan of 125 MEUR signed December 2023 (submarine cable, EIB-led); EU top-up grant 27 MEUR (December 2023); World Bank credit of 270 MUSD under board examination 21 June 2023 (L'Economiste Maghrébin, H. Marzouk, 2023-06-19).
Tunisian Ministry of Industry communiqué via L'Economiste Maghrébin (2026-01-24): capacity of 600 MW, ongoing coordination with Italy; project placed under specific government follow-up (2026-01-27).
